title: Disaggregated expert-parallel serving becomes the default for 2T MoE by H1 2027
body: The open-weight parameter race has produced models—Moonshot's Kimi K3 at 2.8 trillion parameters, Alibaba's Qwen3.8 at 2.4 trillion—that almost nobody can serve with a single-pool setup, and this week the two dominant open inference engines shipped the machinery to run them. SGLang's v0.6.0 leads on wide expert parallelism, spreading a mixture-of-experts model's hundreds of experts across many GPUs, paired with prefill-decode disaggregation, which puts the compute-bound prompt phase on one GPU pool and the bandwidth-bound generation phase on another and ships the KV cache between them over the network through backends like Mooncake and NIXL. vLLM's v0.25.0 landed the same two capabilities within days, the feature-parity-then-race-on-constants cadence these projects have held all year. On a GB200 NVL72 rack the split-pool design already reports roughly 2.7 times the throughput of a single-pool baseline for a trillion-parameter-class MoE. The prediction is that this configuration stops being an advanced opt-in and becomes the default path for 2-trillion-parameter open MoE. By H1 2027 the disaggregated, wide-expert-parallel recipe is the reference deployment both SGLang and vLLM document first for these models, and at least one rentable managed inference offering serves a 2T-class open model with disaggregation switched on by default. The force behind the call is economic rather than technical. With the weights free, the cost of running one of these models is governed almost entirely by whether an operator can stand up disaggregated, expert-parallel serving at all; a 2.4-trillion-parameter checkpoint that cannot be served efficiently undercuts a frontier API only on paper, and the release that makes it servable on a rack you can rent is the one that actually moves the cost curve. Once the cheapest way to run the largest open models is the split-pool recipe, the ecosystem converges on it as the standard, much as tensor parallelism became the unspoken default for dense models a generation earlier. What would falsify this is a simpler winner. If a single-pool or purely tensor-parallel setup stays the documented default for 2T-class open MoE through H1 2027, or if disaggregation remains a hand-tuned, expert-only option rather than the recommended recipe, the call is wrong.

reasoning.because: SGLang v0.6.0 and vLLM v0.25.0 both shipped wide expert-parallel, disaggregated serving this week
reasoning.given: Free weights make serving efficiency the cost driver for 2T open MoE, rewarding one standard recipe
reasoning.so_that: So disaggregated expert-parallel serving becomes the default both engines and a rented platform ship for 2T open MoE
reasoning.landing: by H1 2027; both SGLang and vLLM plus one rented platform default to it
reasoning.plain_language: These giant free AI models are too big to run simply, so spreading the work across many chips becomes the normal way to serve them.

summary: SGLang v0.6.0 and vLLM v0.25.0 both shipped wide expert-parallel, disaggregated serving this week for 2-trillion-parameter open MoE models. With the weights free, serving efficiency sets cost, so this split-pool recipe should become the default both engines and a rented platform ship by H1 2027.
